page: Amazon Web Services i7i.12xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the Intel Xeon 8559C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 3.2 GHz. The processor includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated integer and vector operations. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

This instance is bundled with 11,250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, making it highly suitable for data-intensive operations. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 28 Gbps. The absence of a dedicated GPU is offset by the high-density local storage and high-speed memory subsystem.

In benchmark testing, the i7i.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, as well as image processing. Memory bandwidth tests for both read and write operations place the instance in the top 25% tier, supported by its DDR5 architecture. It also shows strong performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. Large language model inference speeds are strong for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, though text generation on large models falls into the average category.

Given its substantial local NVMe SSD capacity and high memory-to-core ratio, the i7i.12xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for workloads requiring high IOPS and large memory footprints. It is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, data warehousing, real-time analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
